input.quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer to Vendor for late payment, which the playbook prohibits. The amount (15% of annual Fees per week of delay) is punitive and would rapidly exceed the remaining contract value, putting it in walk-away territory; it also sits uneasily with the dispute-withholding right in 7.3 and the mutual liability cap in 21.1 (which expressly does not limit Fee obligations). No Customer-payable early-termination or minimum fee appears elsewhere (Sections 9 and 21 are clean), so the single fix is to strike the LD and substitute ordinary late-payment interest as Vendor's sole remedy.

ops.oldText: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
ops.newText: 7.7 If a proper, undisputed invoice is not paid within thirty days after its due date, Vendor's sole remedy is simple interest on the overdue amount at the lesser of one percent per month or the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law, accruing from the due date until paid. Customer owes no liquidated damages, penalty, or other similar amount under this Agreement.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have removed the liquidated damages payable by us on late payment (15% of annual Fees per week) and replaced it with simple late-payment interest, since our playbook does not accept liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer and this charge could quickly exceed the remaining contract value. We are happy to discuss the interest rate or a modest fixed late fee if that helps.
proposal.summary: Delete Customer-payable liquidated damages in 7.7 and substitute ordinary late-payment interest.
